newsitem.title: INDIA: India's PM promises to protect women's rights.
newsitem.headline: India's PM promises to protect women's rights.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Friday vowed to protect girls against discrimination and promote women in politics, saying society cannot progress if their rights are not protected.
Gujral, delivering a nationally televised address on the 50th anniversary of independence, announced that the government would bar doctors from revealing whether a foetus is a girl or boy.
"Legal restrictions will be imposed on doctors from revealing whether the foetus is a boy or a girl," Gujral said from Delhi's Red Fort.

More boys than girls are born in India, where social workers say women sometimes choose abortion to avoid having a girl child who could later weigh on the family's finances because of the heavy cost of dowry.

Gujral announced a special fund for girls in poor families. "People below the poverty line will get state assistance at the birth of a girl child. When the girl starts attending school, the government will give a scholarship," he said.
The prime minister, whose coalition is split over a bill that would set aside one third of parliament's seats for women, said females should have equal democratic rights.
"Women should be given their right in a country's democracy. They must be given right to enter politics," he said.
"Our democracy has still not given women their right in society. The biggest achievement has been 100,000 women elected to local bodies."

The bill setting aside seats for women in parliament is opposed by some of Gujral's partners in his 15-party centre-left coalition who argue that the measure should also promote the interests of the poor.
Gujral said no country could advance unless women were given equal social, political and economic rights.
"The nation will progress provided both men and women move together shoulder to shoulder," he said.
